questions.question: At the annual general meeting, the shareholders of a company:
options: Manage the daily operations of the company
Prepare the annual financial statements
Elect the directors and appoint the independent auditor
Declare the dividend for the year

questions.question: A director's fiduciary duty means the director must:
options: Act in good faith, in the best interests of the company, and declare any personal interest in a decision
Guarantee shareholders a dividend every year
Own at least half the company's shares
Repay the company's debts personally if it fails

questions.question: An independent non-executive director is valuable to a board because that director:
options: Works in the company every day and knows its operations best
Is a major shareholder with the most to lose
Sets his or her own remuneration
Has no other financial ties to the company, so his or her judgement is not compromised

questions.question: Good governance prefers the chairperson and the chief executive to be different people because:
options: The law forbids one person from holding two titles
One runs the board and the other runs the company — combining them concentrates power that governance exists to divide
It halves the remuneration bill
Shareholders cannot vote for the same person twice

subtopics.title: The King Code and Its Four Demands

questions.question: The King Code is best described as:
options: An Act of Parliament that directors can be imprisoned for breaking
A South African code of good governance practice, which the JSE requires listed companies to apply and explain in their reporting
A tax regulation issued by SARS
An internal policy each company writes for itself

questions.question: A board that hides a large loss from shareholders has primarily violated:
options: Fairness only
Professional competence
Confidentiality
Transparency — and accountability with it, because the board must report openly and answer for results

questions.question: Fairness, as the King Code demands it, requires the board to:
options: Weigh the legitimate interests of all stakeholders — minority shareholders, employees, creditors, customers and the community
Treat every decision as a vote among executive directors
Pay all employees identical salaries
Always follow the wishes of the largest shareholder

questions.question: Directors' pay is set by a remuneration committee and then disclosed in the annual report so that:
options: Directors can keep their earnings confidential
The external auditor can approve each salary
Directors do not set their own pay, and shareholders can weigh that pay against performance
SARS can collect the correct tax

subtopics.title: Professional Ethics and the Code of Conduct

questions.question: A financial director instructed to record January sales in December should refuse, on the principle of:
options: Integrity — the statements must be straightforward and honest, and would no longer fairly present
Confidentiality
Professional behaviour only
Fairness to competitors

questions.question: A director whose spouse's company is bidding for a contract should:
options: Vote for the spouse's company only if its quote is the cheapest
Say nothing, provided the spouse's quote is competitive
Declare the interest and withdraw from the decision, leaving the remaining directors to decide on merit
Resign from the board immediately

questions.question: A director who sells shares after learning of an unpublished profit collapse has committed:
options: Share-price manipulation
Insider trading — trading on information the market lacks, which is illegal
A breach of professional competence
Nothing wrong, because the shares were legally owned

questions.question: Share-price manipulation differs from insider trading in that manipulation involves:
options: Buying shares in a competitor
Trading honestly but in very large volumes
Selling shares before the annual general meeting
Spreading false information or arranging trades to move the price artificially

subtopics.title: Internal Control, Internal Audit and the Independent Audit

questions.question: Division of duties is an internal control measure because:
options: It reduces the number of employees needed
It lets the external auditor skip testing
It guarantees no errors will ever occur
The person who orders is not the person who pays or records, so one person cannot both commit and conceal

questions.question: Internal audit reports its findings to the audit committee rather than only to line managers so that:
options: The findings reach shareholders directly
A finding that embarrasses a manager cannot be buried by that manager
The external audit becomes unnecessary
Managers are never told about weaknesses

questions.question: The independent (external) auditor is appointed by, and reports to:
options: The board of directors
The audit committee
The shareholders, with an opinion on whether the financial statements fairly present the company's position
The internal audit department

questions.question: Lucrative extra consulting work for an audit client threatens the audit because it:
options: Endangers the auditor's independence, on which the value of the audit opinion depends
Takes time away from the audit fieldwork
Is forbidden by the shareholders' resolution
Increases the audit fee beyond the approved amount

questions.question: In the Phambili United picture, the club's members correspond to a company's:
options: Shareholders — they own it, elect those who run it, and can vote them out
Directors
Internal auditors
Creditors

questions.question: The members hand the committee the daily running of the club, but they keep:
options: The bank card and the kit orders
Nothing — election transfers all power permanently
Only the right to attend matches
The votes, the yearly report-back, the right to question the treasurer, and the choice of an outside checker

questions.question: The treasurer's rand is not the treasurer's because:
options: The bank legally owns all deposited money
Every cent belongs to the members who trusted the committee with it — power is held on their behalf
Treasurers may not be paid
The outside accountant controls the account

questions.question: The club's yearly gathering mirrors a company's annual general meeting because it is where:
options: The committee sets its own pay
New members pay their joining fees
Owners hear the report-back, ask hard questions, and elect or remove those who run things
The fixtures for the season are decided

subtopics.title: House Rules That Keep the Money Clean

questions.question: Gate money banked the same day and the leaking roof fixed before it ruins the kit are examples of:
options: Transparency
Fairness
Responsibility — the committee looking after what the club owns
Confidentiality

questions.question: The simple test of accountability in the club is:
options: Whether the committee reports only its successes
Whether anyone spends money and answers to nobody
Whether the first team wins its league
Whether the treasurer is related to any supplier

questions.question: A committee that reports the good months but stays silent about the bad ones has broken:
options: Professional competence
Responsibility
Fairness
Transparency — the books must be open, and hiding is where scandals start

questions.question: The clean remedy for Sello's kit contract to his brother's shop is:
options: Declare the family connection, step out of the decision, gather three quotes, and minute the choice and reasons
Cancel the contract and ban the brother's shop permanently
Allow the deal, provided the price is reasonable
Keep the deal secret but reduce the order size

questions.question: Two signatures on the club account and gate money counted, recorded and banked by different members are:
options: The independent audit
Internal controls — everyday habits that stop one person moving money alone, and protect honest people too
The work of the outside accountant
Requirements of the King Code's fairness demand

questions.question: Naledi reports the gaps she finds to the club's oversight group, not privately to the treasurer, because:
options: A report handed only to the person it embarrasses tends to disappear
The treasurer is too busy to read reports
Members may never speak to the committee directly
The oversight group pays her fee

questions.question: The outside accountant differs from Naledi in that the outside accountant:
options: Works inside the club all year round
Tests the club's habits and controls month by month
Is chosen by the members, has no ties to anyone in the club, and tells the members whether the treasurer's report fairly shows the truth
Reports privately to the committee

questions.question: The three-move method for any governance scenario question is:
options: Quote, compare, judge
Debit, credit, balance
Accuse, dismiss, prosecute
State the problem from the facts, name the principle or duty broken, recommend the remedy that closes it
